thread:
sam_w: Noticing a big spike in tx timeouts on multi-GPU jobs in eu-west after last night's kernel rollout. NCCL jobs stall and then abort with peer reset.

infra_oncall: Yep, dashboards show a ~3x tail latency for p2p allreduce and an uptick in mlx5 tx_timeouts on several hosts.

mike: Quick paste of dmesg from one host: 
```
[ 1234.567890] mlx5_core 0000:3b:00.0: QP 0x1a2b3c tx timeout, resetting port
[ 1234.568012] mlx5_core 0000:3b:00.0: mlx5_fpga: completion handler: ibv_post_send failed -6
[ 1234.568120] ib_core: device 3b:00.0 aborting QP 0x1a2b3c state=ERR
```

elaine: I grepped the control-plane logs and noticed node replacements around the same timestamps. Autoscaler was spinning up replacements for preempted VMs and reusing the same instance IPs within ~30s.

naga: Could be QP reuse / stale MAD/GRH entries after fast node churn. If a new node takes an IP that recently had active QPs, fabric still has cached QPN->path until the stale MAD TTL expires, leading to misdelivered frames and tx timeouts. We saw similar behavior last year but not triggered by autoscaler so fast.

mike: Also found `ibv_devinfo` differences pre/post: new hosts show different uar/mkey sequence numbers (driver reg changed). Combined with reuse this could cause failed registrations and ERRing QPs.

infra_oncall: Packet counters: port 0 tx_timeouts +762 in 10m, rx_errors negligible. Seems transmit side gives up waiting for ACKs.

sam_w: Repro steps we ran: 1) force-reprovision 2 nodes in same rack; 2) start nccl p2p job across them; 3) observe tx timeout within 2-4 minutes. If we wait ~5-10m after reprovisioning, issues stop.

elaine: Short-term mitigation: avoid reusing IPs immediately during autoscale (increase IP cooldown to 10m) and throttle replacements in eu-west. Also add drain+ibv_unbind step before retiring NICs.

rachel_s: Ops/Cost note: throttling replacements will increase queue times and we may have to keep a small spare pool (hot standbys) in eu-west for 48h. Estimated +12% infra spend for that region this week.

naga: Hotfix we applied on one pod: `modprobe -r mlx5_core && modprobe mlx5_core` to reset driver and clear stale QPs — that brought jobs back quickly. Not ideal at scale.

mike: Long-term: we should add a QP cleanup handshake in our deprovision flow, or ensure unique ephemeral IPs per instance lifecycle. Also split autoscaler to prefer different subnets for immediate replacements.

sam_w: Action items: 
- @infra_oncall add IP cooldown to autoscaler config and throttle eu-west replacements (P0)
- @devops schedule driver-reset runbook and a rolling test on canary pool (P1)
- @product/infrastructure approve temporary hot-standby capacity (P2)
- @research investigate whether kernel patch in 6.5.x changed QP/TID reuse timing (P2)

deploy-bot: Canary kernel rollout 6.5.12 -> 6.5.13 completed eu-west-1 at 02:12 UTC last night.

rachel_s: I'll spin up cost estimate doc and ping finance.

infra_oncall: I'll implement cooldown and start a small runbook for `modprobe` workaround. Will post PR link when ready. :thumbsup:

sam_w: Thanks — please paste logs/PRs here. If any cluster shows >5% job failures keep the pager on.
